nodes.label: CONTRACTS.md — API & Data Contracts (authoritative)
nodes.rationale: Declared authoritative: Phase 2 (backend) and Phase 3 (frontend) build against this document; implementation disagreements lose until amended here first.

nodes.label: brain-api (identity authority + BFF)
nodes.rationale: Owns users/tenants/entitlements/demo_requests in its own brain database; the single identity + entitlement authority for the mesh. No browser ever calls precheck/secretaria directly — brain-api fronts them.

nodes.label: secretarIA service
nodes.rationale: Internal-only: no browser, no human, no JWT ever reaches it. Has no user/role system — its only privileged surface is /admin/* behind a shared secret.

nodes.label: PreCheck service
nodes.rationale: Mints its own minimal token (integer sub + exp, separate users table and DB). Design goal: no PreCheck code change — it validates brain-minted SSO tokens with its existing auth unchanged.

nodes.label: brain-frontend unified portal
nodes.rationale: Serves the ported PreCheck app same-origin at /dashboard, so the minted SSO token can be written straight to localStorage — no token ever appears in a URL/Referer/log.

nodes.label: Brain JWT (HS256 access token)
nodes.rationale: Claims sub (user UUID) / tenant_id / role / iat / exp only — no entitlements, secrets, or plan flags in the token (auth-jwt-multitenant rule); product access is resolved server-side at request time. Tokens carrying a scope claim are rejected by every user-facing dependency: scoped service tokens are not user sessions.

nodes.label: Shared SECRET_KEY invariant (brain-api ↔ PreCheck)
nodes.rationale: brain-api SECRET_KEY must be byte-identical to PreCheck's; this is the ONLY coupling between the services and is what lets SSO work with zero PreCheck code change. If they differ, PreCheck rejects the minted token with 401.

nodes.label: POST /sso/precheck/token — PreCheck SSO mint
nodes.rationale: Does not reuse the brain JWT (UUID sub is not a drop-in for PreCheck's integer sub); instead mints a second PreCheck-shaped token, gated on entitlement (403 precheck_not_entitled) and an account link (409 precheck_account_not_linked). TTL matches PreCheck's own 60-min session because the minted token BECOMES the PreCheck session.

nodes.label: precheck_account_links table (SSO identity map)
nodes.rationale: Maps brain user UUID → PreCheck integer user id; the only thing authorizing an SSO mint. precheck_user_id is a logical reference into PreCheck's separate DB with NO foreign key by design (cross-database FKs are impossible).

nodes.label: Refresh-token rotation (refresh_tokens, /auth/refresh, /auth/logout)
nodes.rationale: Rotate-on-use with reuse detection: replaying an already-rotated token revokes the user's entire refresh family. Stored only as sha256 hashes so a DB read never yields a usable credential; logout always returns 204 to avoid a token-existence oracle.

nodes.label: Auth/demo rate limiting (core/ratelimit.py)
nodes.rationale: In-process per-IP sliding window, deliberately fail-open: best-effort anti-abuse must never 500 when the limiter backend is unavailable, since no Redis is in play.

nodes.label: GET /entitlements — resolved entitlement state
nodes.rationale: The single source of truth the portal calls to decide which products to show; resolved in-process from the local row, NEVER calls Stripe. Returns a coherent default instead of 404 for a tenant with no row so the portal always renders.

nodes.label: Plan catalog (services/catalog.py)
nodes.rationale: Single source of truth for everything commercial — plan/add-on ids, product flags, limits, Stripe price placeholders; nothing else hardcodes a plan flag or price. Unknown/stale plan strings resolve to no plan so gates fail closed.

nodes.label: is_entitled gate (services/entitlements.py)
nodes.rationale: The one helper every gate reuses; pure and in-process (no network, no Stripe). Tiers are cumulative; an unknown key raises ValueError — loud programmer error, never a silent deny/grant.

nodes.label: POST /demo-requests — isolated lead capture
nodes.rationale: Deliberately isolated: creates no tenant, touches no entitlements, calls no Stripe, triggers no async work; separate from PreCheck's pre-existing demo funnel.

nodes.label: /admin/* platform-admin API
nodes.rationale: Router-level require_role(admin) gate before any handler runs; admins have tenant_id=null and act across tenants. The destructive secretaria reset is double-guarded (admin gate + explicit confirm:true body).

nodes.label: Modo médico impersonation (POST /admin/impersonate/token)
nodes.rationale: Admin SSO is intentionally not wired (admins have no tenant); this is the one deliberate exception — an admin acts AS a configured demo clinic's doctor via an ordinary tenant-scoped token, so all existing doctor guards and SSO work unchanged. Every mint is WARNING-audited; the token itself is never logged.

nodes.label: /doctor/* tenant doctor API
nodes.rationale: Gated by require_doctor (tenant role + tenant_id present). The acting tenant is ALWAYS taken from the validated token — tenant_id is never accepted as a query/body param, so a doctor cannot read another tenant's data by forging an id.

nodes.label: PreCheck read proxy (forwarded brain JWT)
nodes.rationale: Forwards the caller's brain JWT verbatim; PreCheck validates and scopes it itself — no separate internal key, the same token that authorized the brain-api route authorizes the upstream call. Unset base URL degrades to an empty stub page so the portal keeps rendering locally.

nodes.label: brain-api → secretaria admin connection (X-Admin-Token)
nodes.rationale: secretaria has no user system, so a brain admin cannot SSO in; brain-api calls secretaria's /admin/* on the admin's behalf presenting SECRETARIA_ADMIN_TOKEN — nothing from the caller is forwarded. A destructive-endpoint secret, never logged; unset config fails 503 before any network call.

nodes.label: SECRETARIA_API_KEY / INTERNAL_API_KEY pair key (X-Internal-Api-Key)
nodes.rationale: One secret, two directions: brain-api → secretaria /internal/* AND secretaria → brain-api /internal/*. Must equal secretaria's INTERNAL_API_KEY byte-for-byte; unset on either side degrades the data path to an empty page (inbound fails closed 403), while a mismatch surfaces as 502 — a key problem is never mis-reported as the doctor's own 401. Compared constant-time, never logged.

nodes.label: Doctor data path: brain-api → secretaria /internal (§12.1)
nodes.rationale: Third distinct service-to-service shape: nothing from the caller is forwarded (secretaria has no notion of the user); the tenant rides in the URL path filled from principal.tenant_id. Unconfigured mesh degrades to {data:[], stub:true}; a genuinely failing upstream collapses to a generic 502 — secretaria's body is never surfaced.

nodes.label: secretarIA hub token + introspection (§12.2)
nodes.rationale: Purpose-scoped JWT (scope=secretaria_hub) so no user JWT ever reaches secretarIA; brain-api's own principal dependency rejects scoped tokens. secretarIA never validates locally — it introspects via /internal/secretaria/hub-token/verify, and the entitlement is re-read LIVE each time so a cancellation locks the hub within the 60s cache TTL; secretarIA fails closed on any error.

nodes.label: Usage-event metering (POST /internal/usage-events + usage_events table)
nodes.rationale: The event id is the CALLER's own idempotency key (e.g. reminder:24h:<appointment_id>); the ledger row and the entitlements.usage increment commit in ONE transaction so marker and counter can never drift. Replay returns recorded:false, never an HTTP error; no Stripe call on this path — meter forwarding is a later billing round.

nodes.label: POST /internal/precheck-handoff — secretarIA → PreCheck patient handoff (§12.3)
nodes.rationale: Pre-seeds a PreCheck session for a WhatsApp patient so PreCheck's keyword-matching bootstrap on the first message is skipped. Entitlement-gated BEFORE any upstream call (403 precheck_not_entitled). Unlike the read proxies, an unconfigured mesh fails LOUD (503 precheck_handoff_not_configured, no degrade) — a handoff that silently doesn't happen is worse than a loud failure, since secretarIA has no other way to know the session was never seeded. Single orchestration hop: no DB write, no new local state; errors are brain-api's own generic details, never PreCheck's raw body.

nodes.label: Hub-and-spoke orchestration (brain-api as hub)
nodes.rationale: secretarIA never calls PreCheck directly: brain-api is the identity/entitlement authority, so the PreCheck-entitlement rule lives in exactly one place with no way to drift out of sync (PreCheck is deliberately never asked to re-check it). The hub reuses both spokes it already maintains — the SECRETARIA_API_KEY inbound and the PRECHECK_INTERNAL_TOKEN outbound — avoiding a third pairwise service credential.

nodes.label: PRECHECK_INTERNAL_TOKEN service credential (X-Internal-Token)
nodes.rationale: A separate service credential distinct from the forwarded-brain-JWT proxy pattern; used for the LGPD privacy legs (degrades to skipped_unconfigured when empty) and the patient handoff (fails LOUD 503 when empty — deliberately different degradation semantics per surface).

nodes.label: Stripe billing — checkout, portal, webhook recompute (§13)
nodes.rationale: Three concerns never conflated: entitlement (local row, reads never call Stripe), billing (Stripe), metering (future). The signature-verified webhook is the ONLY writer of plan/status/addons/limits — the client never says what it paid; unknown Stripe statuses map to inactive (fail closed); unset webhook secret fails CLOSED 400.

nodes.label: processed_stripe_events idempotency table
nodes.rationale: PK is the Stripe event.id (natural dedupe key); inserted in the SAME transaction as the entitlement mutation so a failed apply rolls the marker back and Stripe's redelivery legitimately reprocesses.

nodes.label: LGPD privacy orchestration (/admin/privacy/erasure + /export)
nodes.rationale: Brain leg runs first and is the only leg that can refuse the whole operation (409 admin_cannot_be_erased, before any upstream call or audit row). Fan-out legs never block each other; partial is still HTTP 200 and the caller simply retries the same request. No upstream response body is ever surfaced on failure.

nodes.label: privacy_requests audit table
nodes.rationale: One row per invocation, surviving the erasure it records — proof a request was honored without the row itself being personal data: subject stored only as sha256 of the normalized key, result is counts + per-service status only, requested_by is ON DELETE SET NULL so the row outlives the admin account.

hyperedges.label: secretarIA → brain-api → PreCheck patient handoff flow (§12.3)
